artists.biography: David Longdon (born in Nottingham on 17 June 1965; died 20 November 2021) was a British multi-instrumentalist and singer, who was best known as the lead vocalist and co-songwriter of the progressive rock band Big Big Train. Besides singing, Longdon played flute, keyboards, acoustic and electric 6 & 12 string guitars, bass, mandolin, lute, banjo, accordion, percussion, dulcimer, psaltry, vibraphone, theremin and glockenspiel. Longdon began writing music at age nine after discovering The Who. He began his career as the lead singer of the band The Gift Horse. Longdon was one of those who auditioned as lead singer of rock band Genesis in 1996, following the departure of Phil Collins. He auditioned during the making of Calling All Stations (1997), but the role was given to Scottish singer Ray Wilson. He joined Big Big Train in 2009, and performed on numerous instruments in addition to his role as the lead singer beginning with the album The Underfall Yard in 2010. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Wild River" is the debut solo album by English rock musician David Longdon, originally released in 2004. The album showcases Longdon's distinctive blend of melodic rock, progressive elements, and folk influences, marked by rich vocal harmonies, intricate instrumentation, and thoughtful songwriting. Released on the labels Plane Groovy and English Electric Recordings, "Wild River" features a warm, organic sound that highlights Longdon's skills as a multi-instrumentalist and his ability to craft accessible yet musically sophisticated songs.

As Longdon's first solo venture outside his work with Big Big Train, "Wild River" holds a significant place in his discography, offering a more intimate and personal musical statement compared to his band projects. The album was initially self-released in limited quantities, making it a sought-after item among fans. While it did not achieve widespread commercial success upon its original release, "Wild River" was well-received by critics and listeners for its melodic depth and craftsmanship, establishing Longdon as a compelling solo artist within the progressive rock scene.
